user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure tools are installed: `git`, `git-svn`, `svn`
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

---

## Phase 1 — Preparation (9:00–10:00 AM)

### 1.1 Audit the SVN Repo
```bash
# Check repo size and revision count
svn info https://your-svn-repo/url
svn log https://your-svn-repo/url | grep "^r" | wc -l
```

### 1.2 Build an Authors File
SVN uses usernames; Git needs name + email.

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors
svn log https://your-svn-repo/url -q \
  | grep "^r" \
  | awk -F'|' '{print $2}' \
  | sort -u \
  | sed 's/ //g' > authors.txt
```

Edit `authors.txt` into this format:
```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
```

### 1.3 Identify Repo Layout
```bash
# Standard layout?
svn ls https://your-svn-repo/url
# Look for: trunk/ branches/ tags/
```

---

## Phase 2 — Clone SVN → Git (10:00 AM–12:00 PM)

### Standard Layout
```bash
git svn clone https://your-svn-repo/url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -s my-project
```

### Non-Standard Layout (trunk only)
```bash
git svn clone https://your-svn-repo/url/trunk \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  my-project
```

> ⏱️ **Time varies** — small repos (< 1,000 revisions) usually finish in minutes.

---

## Phase 3 — Clean Up the Git Repo (12:00–1:00 PM)

### 3.1 Convert SVN Branches & Tags
```bash
cd my-project

# Convert remote SVN branches to local Git branches
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v "tags/" | grep -v trunk); do
  git branch "${branch##*/}" "$branch"
done

# Convert SVN tags to real Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/"); do
  git tag "${tag##*/tags/}" "$tag"
  git branch -d -r "$tag"
done
```

### 3.2 Remove git-svn Tracking Refs
```bash
git branch -d -r trunk
git config --remove-section svn-remote.svn
rm -rf .git/svn
```

### 3.3 Add a .gitignore
```bash
# SVN uses svn:ignore — convert it
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Add .gitignore from SVN ignore properties"
```

### 3.4 Verify History
```bash
git log --oneline | head -20
git branch -a
git tag
```

---

## Phase 4 — Push to Remote Git Host (1:00–2:00 PM)

```bash
# Create empty repo on GitHub/GitLab first, then:
git remote add origin https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git

# Push all branches and tags
git push origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

---

## Phase 5 — Validation (2:00–3:00 PM)

| Check | Command |
|---|---|
| Commit count matches | `git log --oneline \| wc -l` |
| All authors mapped | `git log --format="%an" \| sort -u` |
| Branches present | `git branch -a` |
| Tags present | `git tag` |
| Latest files correct | `git show HEAD` |

```bash
# Spot-check a specific old revision
git log --all --grep="your known commit message"
```

---

## Phase 6 — Team Cutover (3:00–4:00 PM)

- [ ] **Officially lock SVN** (set to read-only or take offline)
- [ ] Send team the new Git remote URL
- [ ] Share a Git quick-reference cheat sheet
- [ ] Each developer clones fresh:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git
  ```
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines to point to Git
- [ ] Update any documentation/wikis with new repo URL

---

## Phase 7 — Buffer / Troubleshooting (4:00–5:00 PM)

### Common Issues & Fixes

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Unknown author error | Add missing user to `authors.txt`, re-run clone |
| Binary files bloating repo | Consider `git-lfs` post-migration |
| Merge history lost | Expected — SVN merges don't map cleanly to Git |
| Clone hangs/times out | Use `--revision HEAD:1` to clone in reverse |

---

## End-of-Day Summary

```
✅ SVN repo cloned with full history
✅ Authors mapped correctly
✅ Branches and tags converted
✅ Pushed to remote Git host
✅ SVN locked / deprecated
✅ Team notified and cloned
✅ CI/CD updated
```

---

## Keep SVN Available (Read-Only) for 2–4 Weeks
> Gives the team a safety net to reference old diffs before fully decommissioning.

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🔴 Incomplete Author Mapping
**What goes wrong:** Any SVN username missing from `authors.txt` causes the clone to **abort mid-migration**, and commits may be attributed to the wrong people in Git history permanently.

**Mitigation:**
- Run the author extraction script and verify the file is complete *before* cloning
- Use the `--authors-prog` fallback flag to handle unknown users gracefully instead of failing

---

### 2. 🔴 SVN Commits During Migration
**What goes wrong:** If developers keep committing to SVN while the clone is running, the migrated Git repo is **immediately out of date** and a re-run is needed, costing hours.

**Mitigation:**
- Hard-freeze SVN (set to read-only) *before* Phase 2 begins
- Communicate the freeze window clearly the day before

---

### 3. 🟡 Lost or Corrupted Branch & Tag History
**What goes wrong:** SVN branches and tags are just folder copies, not first-class objects. The conversion can produce **broken, duplicate, or missing branches/tags** in Git, especially if the repo used a non-standard layout.

**Mitigation:**
- Audit `svn ls` before migrating to confirm the layout
- Manually verify every branch and tag after Phase 3 before pushing to the remote

## Pre-Migration Checklist

- [ ] Freeze SVN — set to read-only
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository
- [ ] Extract and verify all authors in `authors.txt`
- [ ] Confirm SVN repo layout (`trunk/branches/tags`)
- [ ] Create empty repo on Git host
- [ ] Notify the entire team of the migration window

## Migration Checklist

- [ ] Clone SVN repo with `git svn clone`
- [ ] Convert branches and tags to Git format
- [ ] Generate `.gitignore` from SVN ignore properties
- [ ] Verify commit count and author names
- [ ] Push all branches and tags to remote

## Post-Migration Checklist

- [ ] Lock SVN permanently (or keep read-only for 2–4 weeks)
- [ ] Share new Git remote URL with team
- [ ] Each developer clones the new repo
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines
- [ ] Update documentation and wikis

## Rollback Option

**Keep SVN live and read-only for 2–4 weeks after migration.**

If the Git migration is found to be corrupt or incomplete, the team simply **resumes committing to SVN** as the source of truth, and the migration is re-run from scratch once the issue is resolved.

> **Key requirement:** Do not decommission or delete the SVN repository until the Git repo has been validated and trusted by the whole team.

## Prerequisite

**`git-svn` must be installed on the machine running the migration.**

Without it, the `git svn clone` command is unavailable and the migration cannot start.

```bash
# Verify it is installed
git svn --version
```

> On some systems it is not bundled with Git by default and must be installed separately — for example, `sudo apt install git-svn` on Ubuntu.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
## Fastest Validation Step

**Compare the SVN revision count against the Git commit count.**

```bash
# SVN count
svn log https://your-svn-repo/url -q | grep "^r" | wc -l

# Git count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

> If the two numbers match, the migration captured the full history. Takes under **30 seconds** and immediately confirms whether a deeper investigation is needed.
**9 AM** Freeze SVN → **10 AM** Clone → **12 PM** Clean up → **1 PM** Push → **2 PM** Validate → **3 PM** Team cutover → **5 PM** Done.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
## Two Tools for SVN to Git Migration

### 1. `git-svn`
Built into Git (or installable separately) — clones an SVN repository into Git with full commit history, author mapping, and branch/tag conversion.

### 2. `svn2git`
A Ruby wrapper around `git-svn` that automates the branch and tag cleanup steps, reducing several manual commands into a single one-liner.

```bash
# Example
svn2git https://your-svn-repo/url --authors authors.txt
```

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
## Cutover Approval

**The project or team lead** should approve the final cutover after confirming:

- Commit history looks correct
- All branches and tags are present
- CI/CD pipelines are working against the new Git repo

> No developer should switch to the Git repo as source of truth until this sign-off is given.

## Communication Tip

**Send a single clear message to the whole team the day before**, stating the exact SVN freeze time, the expected cutover time, and the new Git remote URL — so no one is caught off guard or commits to SVN during the migration.

## Final Recap

**Goal:** Move a small SVN repo to Git in one working day with zero history loss.

| Phase | Key Action |
|---|---|
| Prepare | Freeze SVN, map authors, back up |
| Migrate | Clone with `git-svn` or `svn2git` |
| Clean Up | Convert branches, tags, `.gitignore` |
| Validate | Match commit counts, check authors |
| Cutover | Team lead approves, team clones fresh |

**Top 3 Risks:** Incomplete author mapping, commits during migration, broken branches and tags.

**Rollback:** Keep SVN read-only for 2–4 weeks as a safety net.

**Key Prerequisite:** `git-svn` installed and verified before starting.

> A well-communicated freeze window and a complete `authors.txt` file are the two things most likely to make or break the migration.

## Final Recap

- Freeze SVN the night before
- Map all authors in `authors.txt`
- Clone with `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- Convert branches and tags
- Generate `.gitignore`
- Match commit counts to validate
- Team lead approves cutover
- Team clones fresh Git repo
- Update CI/CD and docs
- Keep SVN read-only for 2–4 weeks
